drafts.rationale: Lightest feasible design found. Passes REQ-001 to REQ-007 at nominal and in the REQ-006 worst case (2750 N, 29.5 mm). t/w = 2.00 is at the REQ-007 limit.
Passes all requirements. Ultimate margin in the REQ-006 worst case is only about +0.007, so it has little headroom.
Passes all requirements with lower t/w (0.62) and more margin than the lighter options.
Most conservative of the four. Passes all requirements, with t/w = 0.32 and the largest stiffness margin among these options.

Lightest feasible point. Stiffness governs (REQ-003/006). Worst case (2750 N, 19.5 mm) gives yield MS +0.39, ultimate MS +0.17, deflection 2.98 mm. Width 11 mm fails REQ-006 (3.25 mm), so 12 mm is the minimum at 20 mm thickness. Passes REQ-004/005/007 (t/w 1.67).
Slightly wider than the lightest point for extra stiffness margin. Worst case gives yield MS +0.45, deflection 2.86 mm. Passes all requirements, t/w 1.60.
Thicker plate gives much larger stiffness margin. Worst case gives yield MS +1.29, deflection 1.44 mm. t/w is exactly 2.00, at the REQ-007 limit. Passes all requirements.
Alternative thickness. Worst case gives yield MS +0.76, ultimate MS +0.48, deflection 2.97 mm. Heavier than the 20 mm options. Passes all requirements, t/w 0.67.
Lightest passing design. Yield stress 269 MPa nominal (MS +0.29). Worst case REQ-006 (2750 N, 24.5 mm) gives MS +0.13 and 0.80 mm. t/w = 2.00, at the REQ-007 limit. Stock thickness 25 mm.
Same thickness with 0.5 mm more width for more margin. Worst case REQ-006 gives MS +0.18 and 0.77 mm. t/w = 1.92, so REQ-007 holds with some slack.
Alternative using 20 mm stock. Nominal MS +0.16. Worst case REQ-006 gives MS +0.00 and 1.13 mm, which is marginal but passes. t/w = 1.14.
Thinner, wider section for a different trade-off. Nominal MS +0.19. Worst case REQ-006 gives MS +0.01 and 1.41 mm. t/w = 0.57. Heavier than the 25 mm options.
Lightest passing Al design found. Ultimate margin at the REQ-006 robustness case is only +0.010, so it is tight. 15.25 x 30 fails REQ-006 (ultimate MS -0.006).
Same 30 mm thickness with a small width increase for more ultimate margin at the robustness case (+0.19 nominal, +0.04 worst case). Passes all requirements, t/w 1.88.
Thinner, wider alternative at 25 mm stock thickness. Passes all requirements with t/w 1.09, but is heavier than the 30 mm options.
Thick-and-wide alternative at 20 mm stock thickness. Passes all requirements with t/w 0.56, but is the heaviest of the four.
Lightest verified passing design. Yield MS +0.62 nominal, deflection 2.50 mm nominal, robustness MS +0.40 at 2.97 mm. t/w 1.48 meets REQ-007. Thin deflection margin under the +10% load case.
Verified pass. Yield MS +0.68 nominal, deflection 2.41 mm nominal, robustness MS +0.45 at 2.86 mm. t/w 1.43. Slightly heavier but more deflection margin than 13.5 x 20.
Verified pass. Yield MS +0.80 nominal, deflection 2.25 mm nominal, robustness MS +0.55 at 2.67 mm. t/w 1.33. Heavier, with more margin on stress and deflection.

Verified pass. Yield MS +1.34 nominal, deflection 1.38 mm nominal, robustness MS +1.04 at 1.62 mm. t/w exactly 2.00, so REQ-007 has no margin. Heaviest of the four, included as the high-margin option.
Lightest passing Steel design found. Passes REQ-001 to REQ-007; REQ-006 worst-case MS +0.01 (tight). Width is the minimum that satisfies REQ-007 (t/w = 2.0) at 25 mm thickness.
Passes all requirements with more robustness margin than 12.5 x 25 (REQ-006 worst-case MS +0.05). t/w = 1.92. Slightly heavier fallback.
Passes all requirements. Square section with t/w = 1.0; REQ-006 worst-case MS +0.02. Heavier, but an alternative geometry if the 25 mm plate is undesirable.
Passes all requirements with the most margin (REQ-006 worst-case MS +0.76, deflection 0.43 mm). Heaviest of the four; t/w = 2.0 at the REQ-007 limit.

attacks.title: Heavier payload (+25%, 3500 N)
attacks.rationale: Stress test shows deflection rises to 3.126 mm, exceeding the 3 mm limit (REQ-003). Strength still passes (yield MS 0.293, ultimate MS 0.091). Deflection scales linearly with load, so stiffness headroom is only about +20% in load.

attacks.title: Longer arm (+10 mm, 150 mm)
attacks.rationale: Stress test shows deflection reaches 3.076 mm, exceeding the 3 mm limit (REQ-003). Deflection scales with length cubed, so the arm can grow only about 6% (to roughly 149 mm) before REQ-003 fails.

attacks.title: REQ-006 combined case (+10% load, 0.5 mm thinner plate)
attacks.rationale: Passes, but barely: yield MS 0.397, ultimate MS 0.178, deflection 2.968 mm against 3.0 mm. The 19.5 mm thickness is not a stock size (REQ-005), and the next stock size down (16 mm) fails by hand calculation (ultimate MS about -0.13, deflection about 4.9 mm). Width also has almost no slack: about 13.4 mm is needed for REQ-003 under this case, versus 13.5 mm in the design.

attacks.title: Machining loss (1 mm thickness)
attacks.rationale: Passes: deflection 2.917 mm, yield MS 0.459, ultimate MS 0.230. Headroom is small: thickness can lose only about 1.2 mm (minimum about 18.8 mm) before deflection exceeds 3 mm. Assumes tight machining tolerance.

attacks.title: Machining loss (1.5 mm width, to 12 mm)
attacks.rationale: Passes: deflection 2.813 mm, yield MS 0.437, ultimate MS 0.212. Width can lose only about 2.25 mm (minimum about 11.25 mm) before deflection exceeds 3 mm. REQ-004 floors width at 10 mm, and REQ-007 (thickness/width <= 2) would fail at 10 mm with 20 mm thickness.

events.rationale: No finding is blocking: G-01 gives 0.05% probability of failure against the 1% limit, G-02 and G-03 show margin beyond the required +10% load and -0.5 mm thinning, and G-05 reports no untestable risks. The 13.5 x 20 mm Ti-6Al-4V bracket meets REQ-001 to REQ-007 with margin, and G-04's two confirmed attacks (3500 N payload, 150 mm arm) lie outside the requirement envelope, so they are carried as open conditions rather than grounds to redesign.
conditions: Owner: Red Team lead. Document the confirmed out-of-envelope attacks from G-04 (3500 N payload, 150 mm arm) and state the operating limits the part is released to, so users cannot exceed them unknowingly.

Owner: Stress analyst. Confirm the 167 g mass against the lowest-mass goal by comparing against the Al 6061-T6 and Steel 4130 candidates that were not carried forward, and record the result in the release package.
Owner: Quality engineer. Keep the G-01 Monte Carlo tail (5% of parts with governing margin below +0.093) in the production inspection plan and flag any lot falling below that margin.
Owner: Design lead. Verify that the 13.5 x 20 mm section is held to tolerance in drawings, since REQ-006 deflection (about 2.97 mm vs 3 mm) leaves very little room for width or thickness deviation.

events.summary: The Ti-6Al-4V 13.5 x 20 mm bracket passes all six structural and stability rules (S-01 to S-06) and the manufacturing and feasibility checks (M-02 to M-04, F-01 to F-03), with M-06 recorded as info for AMS 4911 annealed plate. Seven rules remain at action status (M-01, M-05, X-01, X-02, P-01, P-02, P-03), and P-04 is info only, so the design is not yet ready for release.
top_risks: X-02: Fatigue is not analyzed, and cyclic load cases such as launch vibration are still needed, so the passing structural margins (S-01 to S-03) do not yet cover fatigue life.

M-01: The design uses typical handbook allowables rather than MMPDS A- or B-basis values for this alloy, temper and thickness, so the margins in S-01 to S-03 may change when the correct allowables are applied.
X-01: The fracture control classification has not been assigned, which leaves the required fracture control rigor and rationale unrecorded.

actions.action: Replace the typical values with MMPDS A- or B-basis allowables for Ti-6Al-4V, the AMS 4911 annealed plate temper and the 20 mm thickness, then rerun S-01 to S-03.
Define cyclic load cases, including launch vibration, and complete a fatigue analysis for the bracket.
Classify the part (for example, non-fracture-critical) per NASA-STD-5019 and record the rationale in the compliance file.
Specify fastener material and finish at the joint to avoid galvanic corrosion per MIL-STD-889.
Require a certificate of conformance and mill test report traceable to the heat lot in the purchase order.
